reasoning: The stateless outer cBPF filter permits execve for the initial bwrap payload handoff. It cannot inspect pathnames or distinguish a later execve.
Writable bind mounts have no demonstrated noexec enforcement. openat can create an executable file there and the same allowed execve can launch it before the main-time filter.
The exposed dynamic ELF interpreter is itself executable. A readonly runtime allowlist alone does not restrict it to the initial probe or authenticate code loaded from writable paths.

Even prospective noexec mounts would require a full executable-mapping review: mmap and mprotect currently admit executable anonymous memory; pathname-only checks do not prove a code-identity boundary.
The probe no-exec filter is installed in main after ELF interpreter/libc initialization. It cannot establish the requested pre-main guarantee.
No filter weakening, namespace fallback, launcher bypass, provenance assertion or execution permit is used to hide this conflict.
